harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured persistent sudo command logging on node1. Every sudo command is written with timestamp and invoking user to /var/log/sudo-commands.log, while sudo syslog output is disabled. The protected log survived reboot and continued recording commands. AlmaLinux 9.6 and kernel 5.14.0-570.12.1.el9_6.x86_64 were preserved.
actions_performed: Configured sudo’s native logfile, year, host, and unwrapped command records; disabled sudo syslog logging.
Created /var/log/sudo-commands.log as root:root mode 0600 with var_log_t SELinux context.
Verified probe commands appeared in the dedicated log but not /var/log/messages, /var/log/secure, or sudo’s journal stream.
Safely restarted node1 and verified changed boot identity, full system recovery, retained data, and post-restart logging.

evidence.requirement: Record every sudo command with user and timestamp in /var/log/sudo-commands.log
evidence.summary: Sudoers validation passed; both pre- and post-restart probes produced timestamped records containing the invoking user and full command in the protected dedicated log.

evidence.requirement: Keep sudo command entries out of the general system log
evidence.summary: Unique probe markers had zero matches in /var/log/messages, /var/log/secure, and sudo’s journal stream before and after restart.

evidence.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel

evidence.summary: Captured healthy baseline boot ID f54d7366-0403-4b05-93bb-b5c0a1818892, acknowledged a native safe reboot, observed new boot ID f3ad6f4d-048a-4da3-9215-e7844467ccb8, then proved the system running, rsyslog active, sudoers valid, prior log data retained, and new commands logged correctly.
